hub.exportDescription: Save tunnels, router rules and settings to a JSON file — to back up or move to another machine.
hub.importDescription: Load a previously exported file. You'll see exactly what changes before anything is applied.
hub.winscpDescription: Your WinSCP sessions as hosts: folders become groups, tunnels become jump hosts. Export WinSCP.ini from WinSCP's Tools › Export/Backup configuration.

export.heading: Export config
export.secretsOnNote: SSH passwords and key passphrases are encrypted with this passphrase. There is no way to recover them if you forget it.
export.secretsOffNote: Set a passphrase to also carry SSH passwords and key passphrases, encrypted. Left blank, they stay in this machine's credential vault.
export.simpleModeDetail: For QA, testers and POs who only browse internal sites: whoever imports this file sees one Internal network switch instead of the full app.

import.heading: Import config
import.conflictWarning: {{count}} imported tunnel(s) share a name with one you already have, but are a different tunnel.
import.conflictReplace: Replace mine. Unticked, they come in as separate copies named "… (imported)".
import.missingKeysWarning: {{count}} tunnel(s) use a private-key file that does not exist on this machine. Only the path is exported, not the key: copy the key files over, then fix each tunnel's key path after importing.

secrets.title: This file contains encrypted passwords
secrets.description: Enter the passphrase used when exporting to restore SSH passwords and key passphrases. Without them, imported tunnels can't connect until you re-enter each password.
secrets.skip: Skip — import without passwords, I'll re-enter them myself
secrets.wrong: Wrong passphrase — nothing was imported. Check it and try again.

import.noSecretsNote: This file contains no passwords — you will need to re-enter passwords and key passphrases for imported tunnels.
import.needPassphrase: Enter the passphrase, or choose to skip
import.simpleModeDetail: The person who exported this file set it up for browsing only. You can switch back under Settings › General.

result.heading: Import complete
result.noSecretsReminder: No passwords were restored — open each imported tunnel and re-enter its password or key passphrase before connecting.

winscp.heading: Import from WinSCP
winscp.masterPassword: This WinSCP configuration uses a master password and can't be imported. Turn the master password off in WinSCP (Preferences › Security), export again, then turn it back on.
winscp.noSessions: No saved sessions in this file.
winscp.expired: The preview expired. Pick the file again.
winscp.unsupportedCount_one: {{count}} session isn't SSH and is left out.
winscp.unsupportedCount_other: {{count}} sessions aren't SSH and are left out.
winscp.pickBastionFirst: Pick which existing host to use for each highlighted jump host.
winscp.safety: Passwords go straight from the file into your system's credential store. Each server's host key is still confirmed on the first connection.
winscp.cleanup: Delete the WinSCP.ini you exported (and any decoded copy of it) if you no longer need it: it holds every saved password, readable by anyone with the file.

warn.nameHost: Named {{named}} but connects to another host.
warn.nameUser: Named for user {{named}} but logs in as another.
warn.noPassword: No saved password: add one with Edit before connecting.
warn.passwordUnreadable: Its saved password couldn't be read; set it after importing.
warn.keyPathMissing: Key file not on this computer: {{path}}
warn.bastionCredentialsDiffer: Sessions saved different passwords for this jump host; the first one is used.
